column3: vt. 剪, 剪取, 删除, 削减;n. 剪刀
column5: The fitter will scissor the sheet metal to match the curved panel.
column6: 装配工会把金属板剪裁成弧形面板的形状。

column3: n. 戏水者, 浅尝者
column5: He remained a dabbler in carpentry, finishing stools but never a cabinet.
column6: 他玩木工始终浅尝辄止,做完凳子却从未完成橱柜。

column3: v. 详细说明, 列举, 使特殊
column5: The auditor asked the manager to particularize each expense claimed on the form.
column6: 审计员要求经理逐项列明表格上申报的每笔开支。

column3: v. 行乞, 乞讨, 贩卖
column5: He would cadge cigarettes from strangers rather than ever buy a pack.
column6: 他宁可向陌生人讨烟抽,也从不自己买一包。

column3: n. 自夸学问的人, 空谈家, 书呆子
column5: Only a pedant would interrupt a wedding toast to correct a date.
column6: 只有书呆子才会在婚宴祝酒时打断别人去纠正日期。

column3: a. 胆怯的, 胆小的, 羞怯的
column5: The timorous intern hesitated before knocking on the editor's glass door.
column6: 胆怯的实习生在敲主编玻璃门时犹豫不决。

column3: n. 虚伪, 谎话, 说谎癖;谎言癖, 谎言
column5: The memoir's central lie exposed the author's habitual mendacity to reviewers.
column6: 回忆录的核心谎言向评论者暴露了作者的惯于撒谎。

column3: v. 预谋, 预先考虑
column5: Prosecutors must prove the suspect did premeditate the crime, not merely react.
column6: 控方必须证明嫌疑人是蓄意犯罪,而非一时冲动。

column3: a. 流行的, 时髦的
column5: The lobby's modish furniture looked dated within five short years.
column6: 大堂时髦的家具短短五年就显得过时了。

column3: vi. 劝诫, 告诫；忠告
column5: The librarian began to expostulate, but the noisy students had already left.
column6: 图书管理员刚要劝阻,吵闹的学生们却已离开。

column3: n. 忘恩者;a. 不知恩的, 忘恩的
column5: Calling him an ingrate seemed harsh, since he never asked for help.
column6: 骂他忘恩负义似乎过分,毕竟他从没求过帮忙。

column3: a. 易怒的, 暴躁的
column5: The testy customer demanded a refund before the clerk could explain.
column6: 暴躁的顾客不等店员解释就要求退款。

column3: n. 戏言, 笑料, 嘲弄;vi. 开玩笑
column5: His classmates played a harmless jape, hiding the teacher's chalk.
column6: 同学们开了个无伤大雅的玩笑,藏起了老师的粉笔。

column3: n. 抗议, 忠告, 规劝;抗议, 抗辩, 规劝
column5: Despite every remonstrance from his doctor, the conductor refused to slow down.
column6: 尽管医生再三劝告,指挥家仍拒绝放慢工作节奏。

column3: n. 仲裁者, 调解人;调解人, 说情者, 从中调解者
column5: The village elder acted as intercessor between the feuding farming families.
column6: 村中长者充当调停人,化解两个农户家族的积怨。

column3: n. 凶恶的老妇, 丑婆, 鬼婆
column5: The sitcom's landlady is a comic harridan who shrieks about unpaid rent.
column6: 情景喜剧里的女房东是个滑稽的泼妇,总为欠租尖叫。

column3: a. 不安定的, 易发生变化的;不稳定的, 易变的
column5: Adolescent moods are notoriously labile, shifting within a single afternoon.
column6: 青春期的情绪极不稳定,一下午之内就能阴晴不定。

column3: n. 谈判, 交涉, 洽商, 废话, 奉承;vi. 唠叨, 拍马屁, 交涉, 用花言巧语骗人
column5: The traders spent hours in palaver before agreeing on the pepper price.
column6: 商人们费了几个小时的口舌才就胡椒价格达成一致。

column3: a. 爱挑剔的, 吹毛求疵的, 精细的
column5: The persnickety director rehearsed the handshake scene eleven consecutive times.
column6: 爱挑剔的导演把握手那场戏连排了十一遍。

column3: n. 顽固分子;顽固分子, 顽固派, 死不屈从者
column5: Only diehard fans stayed until the encore ended after midnight.
column6: 只有铁杆歌迷留到午夜之后安可结束才走。

column3: a. 适当的, 恰当的, 合适的, 好看的
column5: Loud argument at a funeral is neither seemly nor kind.
column6: 在葬礼上大声争吵既不得体也不厚道。

column3: a. 淡而无味的, 令人作呕的, 感伤的
column5: Audiences liked the romance despite critics calling it mawkish and predictable.
column6: 尽管评论家称其矫情老套,观众仍喜爱这部爱情片。

column3: n. 令人扫兴的人, 煞风景
column5: Nobody invited the killjoy who objects to every office celebration.
column6: 没人再请那个反对一切办公室庆祝活动的扫兴鬼。

column3: vt. 掘出, 发掘, 使显露
column5: Curators hope to disinter the time capsule buried during the world fair.
column6: 馆长们希望能挖出世博会期间埋下的时间胶囊。

column3: a. 该咒的, 可憎恨的, 讨厌的
column5: The translation was execrable, rendering the subtle essay nearly incomprehensible.
column6: 译文糟糕透顶,把精妙的文章弄得几乎无法理解。

column3: a. 占优势的, 多数的, 主要的, 突出的
column5: Wheat remains the preponderant crop across the region's gently rolling farms.
column6: 小麦仍是这个地区缓坡农田里的主要作物。

column3: a. 重复的, 赘述的
column5: The definition was tautological, defining patience merely as the quality of being patient.
column6: 这个定义同义反复,只把耐心定义为有耐心的品质。

column3: n. 愉快, 欢乐
column5: The string quartet played for the delectation of the cruise passengers.
column6: 弦乐四重奏为邮轮乘客演奏,供他们赏心悦目。

column3: a. 微光的, 黄昏的, 拂晓的;黄昏的, 朦胧的
column5: Crepuscular animals like deer feed most actively at dawn and dusk.
column6: 鹿等晨昏性动物在黎明和黄昏最为活跃。

column3: vt. 使骨化, 使硬化, 使僵化;vi. 骨化, 硬化, 变得极端保守
column5: Large institutions tend to ossify unless outsiders periodically refresh their leadership.
column6: 大机构容易僵化,除非外部人才定期更新领导层。
